answer:
(1) postgres_changes: enable per table with `alter publication supabase_realtime add table t;` (Dashboard → Publications also works); add `alter table t replica identity full;` if you need old records/filters on DELETE. RLS is enforced per subscriber: "Postgres Changes authorizes every event against each subscriber" — anon subscribers need `GRANT SELECT ... TO anon` plus a `for select to anon using (true)` policy, and only rows their policies allow are delivered. Exception: DELETE events are sent to all subscribers (RLS can't be checked). Scale: changes are processed single-threaded, and N subscribers means N authorization checks per change. Quotas: Free = 200 concurrent connections / 100 msgs/s; Pro = 500/500 (10,000/2,500 with spend cap off). At 1 insert/s × ~300 subscribers you deliver ~300 msgs/s — over Free, at the edge of capped Pro.

(2) Yes, prefer Broadcast — Supabase now explicitly recommends "Broadcast from Database" (an AFTER trigger calling `realtime.broadcast_changes(topic, event, op, table, schema, NEW, OLD)`) over postgres_changes for scalability: one fan-out instead of per-subscriber RLS checks, and auth is checked once at channel join then cached. Requires a private channel (`{config:{private:true}}`) plus a SELECT policy on `realtime.messages` (target `anon` for a public feed). Bonus: Broadcast Replay (public alpha, supabase-js ≥2.74.0) backfills missed messages (`replay:{since,limit≤25}`, ~72h retention) — postgres_changes has no replay.

(3) supabase-py: batch insert = pass a list of dicts to `.insert([...]).execute()`; stats row = `.upsert({...}, on_conflict="col")` (PK is default conflict target; use `returning='minimal'` for a writer). API errors raise postgrest `APIError`; offline you get raw httpx exceptions (`ConnectError`, `ReadTimeout`, `RemoteProtocolError`) — wrap every `execute()` in retry/backoff. Plain PostgREST HTTP via httpx (`POST /rest/v1/t`, headers `apikey` + `Authorization: Bearer`, `Prefer: resolution=merge-duplicates, return=minimal`, `?on_conflict=col`, JSON array = bulk) is a perfectly sane, arguably simpler option for a long-running writer — explicit timeouts, your own retry queue, no client-lib state.

(4) Storage: public bucket → reads bypass RLS (anyone with the URL); uploads/deletes still require policies (irrelevant to your service-key writer, which bypasses). Python: `supabase.storage.from_("clips").upload(path=..., file=f, file_options={"content-type": "video/mp4", "cache-control": "3600"})`; `get_public_url(path)` for the link. Limits: global file cap 50MB Free, configurable to 500GB on paid; standard uploads ≤5GB but recommended <6MB — use TUS above that.

(5) Enable RLS, add only `create policy ... for select to anon, authenticated using (true);` — no insert/update/delete policies = no public writes (RLS default-denies). The service_role/secret key maps to a Postgres role with `bypassrls`; that's fine and intended for your server-side writer — just never ship it to the browser/site.

(6) Next.js: `@supabase/ssr` — `createServerClient` (cookies getAll/setAll) in a Server Component fetches initial rows with the anon/publishable key; pass them as props to a `'use client'` component that uses `createBrowserClient` and subscribes in `useEffect` (cleanup via `supabase.removeChannel`). Reconnection: `subscribe((status, err) => ...)` reports SUBSCRIBED / CHANNEL_ERROR / TIMED_OUT / CLOSED; there is no gap-fill for postgres_changes, so on re-SUBSCRIBED refetch rows newer than the last-seen id/created_at — or use Broadcast Replay with `since = lastSeenTs` to backfill.

facts.claim: Enable postgres_changes per table via `alter publication supabase_realtime add table <table>;` (or Dashboard Publications toggle); `alter table <t> replica identity full;` is required to filter/receive old records on DELETE

"Postgres Changes authorizes every event against each subscriber" — subscribers only receive rows their RLS policies allow; anon access needs GRANT SELECT to anon plus a `for select to anon using (true)` policy
RLS policies are NOT applied to DELETE events — all subscribers receive DELETE events regardless of policies

Postgres Changes are processed on a single thread to preserve order (larger compute doesn't raise throughput); 1 change with 100 subscribers = 100 authorization checks; above ~3,000 concurrent subscribers Supabase says to use Broadcast instead

Realtime quotas: concurrent connections Free 200 / Pro 500 / Pro-no-spend-cap & Team 10,000; messages per second Free 100 / Pro 500 / no-cap & Team 2,500; channel joins/s same tiers; 100 channels per connection; broadcast payload 256KB Free / 3,000KB paid; postgres_changes payload 1,024KB

Realtime message usage counts per recipient: a broadcast to 4 clients = 5 messages (1 sent + 4 received); each database change counts as one message per listening client; $2.50 per million overage; 2M included Free, 5M Pro/Team

Supabase recommends Broadcast (via `realtime.broadcast_changes` trigger) over postgres_changes for scalability and security when subscribing to database changes; client listens on a private channel: `.channel('topic:'+id, { config: { private: true } })` with a SELECT policy on realtime.messages

`realtime.broadcast_changes(topic, event, operation, table, schema, new_record, old_record)` signature (used with TG_OP/TG_TABLE_NAME in an AFTER trigger); `realtime.send(payload, event, topic, is_private)` also exists; broadcast-from-database messages are stored in realtime.messages and deleted after ~3 days

Realtime Authorization: private-channel access is computed when the channel topic is joined and "Client access policies are cached for the duration of the connection" — the database is not queried per message

Broadcast Replay (Public Alpha): channel config `broadcast: { replay: { since: <unix ms>, limit: <1-25> } }`, requires supabase-js ≥ 2.74.0, private channels, and only messages sent via Broadcast from Database; replayed messages carry meta.replayed=true; retention ~72h (partitions dropped after 72h, so 72h–4 days)

supabase-py batch insert: pass a list of dicts — `supabase.table("t").insert([{...},{...}]).execute()`; options include count, returning ('minimal'|'representation', default representation), default_to_null

supabase-py upsert: `.upsert(json, count=None, returning='representation', ignore_duplicates=None, on_conflict=None, default_to_null=None)`; primary key must be included; on_conflict targets a UNIQUE column, PK is the default conflict target
supabase-py raises postgrest `APIError` on API-level errors; connection-level failures surface as httpx exceptions (httpx.RemoteProtocolError, httpx.ConnectError, httpx.ReadTimeout) per issue reports

PostgREST direct HTTP: bulk insert = POST a JSON array; upsert = `Prefer: resolution=merge-duplicates` (or ignore-duplicates) with optional `?on_conflict=col`; `Prefer: return=representation|minimal` controls response body
Public storage buckets bypass access control for retrieving/serving files (anyone with the URL can read; cached better on CDN), but uploads/deletes/moves/copies still enforce policies

supabase-py storage upload: `supabase.storage.from_("bucket").upload(path=..., file=f, file_options={"cache-control":"3600","upsert":"false"})`; content-type defaults to text/html if unspecified; `get_public_url("folder/file.jpg")` returns the public link
Storage global file size limit: 50 MB max on Free, configurable up to 500 GB on paid plans; per-bucket limits can be set lower than the global limit

Standard uploads recommended for files <6MB (hard cap 5GB); TUS resumable uploads recommended above 6MB; overwriting an existing path needs upsert and is discouraged due to CDN propagation/stale content — upload to a new path instead
Public-read RLS pattern: `create policy "..." on public.t for select to anon, authenticated using ( true );` — with RLS enabled and no other policies, writes are denied to public roles

"A secret key authorizes access through the service_role Postgres role, which has the bypassrls attribute"; "Never use a secret key in the browser or expose it to customers"; policy performance: wrap auth functions in (select ...), always use the TO clause, index policy filter columns

Next.js App Router setup: install @supabase/supabase-js + @supabase/ssr; createBrowserClient in utils/supabase/client.ts for Client Components, createServerClient with cookie getAll/setAll in utils/supabase/server.ts for Server Components/Actions/Route Handlers; env vars NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY
channel.subscribe((status, err) => ...) reports exactly: SUBSCRIBED, CHANNEL_ERROR, TIMED_OUT, CLOSED
Realtime delivers postgres changes by polling a logical replication slot and appending subscription IDs to WAL records (no persistence for postgres_changes deliveries is described)
Official guide "Using Realtime with Next.js" covers client- and server-side patterns for receiving postgres changes (video-based)

gotchas: Cost math (derived from documented per-recipient counting): 1 insert/s × 300 subscribers, 24/7 ≈ 26M messages/day ≈ 780M/month → roughly $1,900/month overage at $2.50/M on Pro. This applies to BOTH postgres_changes and broadcast (fan-out is billed per recipient). For a live-commentary feed, coalesce events — e.g. one digest broadcast every 5–10 s — to cut this 5–10×.

Free plan caps at 100 messages/second — 300 concurrent subscribers at 1 event/s exceeds it immediately; Pro with spend cap is 500 msgs/s (2,500 with cap off). Concurrent-connection caps (200 Free / 500 Pro capped) also bite at 'a few hundred' viewers.
postgres_changes leaks DELETE events to every subscriber regardless of RLS — don't rely on RLS to hide deletions.

Broadcast Replay only works on private channels and only for messages sent via Broadcast from Database; plain client/REST broadcasts and postgres_changes cannot be replayed — for those you must refetch missed rows over PostgREST after reconnect (keep a last-seen id/timestamp).

Realtime Authorization docs' example policies on realtime.messages all use `to authenticated`; for an anon-key public feed on a private channel you must write the policy `to anon` — and the docs never explicitly confirm anon-role private-channel joins, so test this before committing to broadcast+replay (fallback: public broadcast channel, losing replay).

Docs pages disagree on key naming: newer pages use publishable/secret keys (NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, sb_secret_...) while older guides and existing projects use anon/service_role JWTs — both currently work, but the RLS-bypass semantics quoted are worded for secret keys.

supabase-py network failures raise raw httpx exceptions, not APIError — a long-running writer must catch (httpx.HTTPError, APIError) broadly, use its own retry queue, and never let one failed insert kill the loop; consider buffering events locally and flushing as batched inserts.

Uploading clips: don't overwrite the same storage path (CDN serves stale content); write each clip/screenshot to a new timestamped path. Content-type defaults to text/html in supabase-py if you forget file_options.
Realtime Authorization caches channel policies for the connection lifetime — RLS changes don't apply to already-connected subscribers until they reconnect.
Adding a table to supabase_realtime publication only affects new WAL entries; also ensure RLS is enabled on the table itself or anon postgres_changes subscribers with a grant get everything.
